## Objective
- Upgrade “The House Within” into a more polished, physically interactive horror game, emphasizing world effects over text notifications.

## Requirements
- Build or modify the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Add lightweight authored physical props and particle effects using the game’s existing Three.js setup.
- Animate door and refrigerator movement instead of teleporting them.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added loose cans, papers, and keys with simple gravity, damping, and player-proximity impulses.
- Added dust motes and particle effects for water, steam, footsteps/disturbances, and door interactions.
- Added eased door and refrigerator animation.
- Wired physical world updates into the render loop.

### Active
- Validate `game.js` syntax and gameplay in-browser; fix any issues.
- Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Check `game.js` for syntax/runtime errors, especially recent edits to refrigerator and event logic.
2. Run the game and verify movement, interactions, animations, and effects.
3. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot; summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing game and all current physical-interaction changes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or screenshot checks have been run.
- A user-facing text “physical effects not text” request remains the guiding design preference.
